results.source: PI-RADS v2.1 (Turkbey et al., Eur Urol 2019)
results.text: PI-RADS 3 lesions are equivocal; the decision to biopsy is commonly informed by additional factors such as PSA density, prior biopsy history and patient preference.

results.source: PI-RADS v2.1 (Turkbey et al., Eur Urol 2019)
results.text: PI-RADS assessment categories express the likelihood of clinically significant cancer: 1 very low, 2 low, 3 intermediate (equivocal), 4 high (likely), 5 very high (highly likely).
When MRI is positive (PI-RADS 3 or higher), MRI-targeted biopsy is recommended, combined with systematic biopsy in biopsy-naive men.
When MRI is negative (PI-RADS 1-2) and clinical suspicion of prostate cancer is low, biopsy may be omitted based on shared decision-making with the patient.

results.source: Schoots et al., BJU Int 2021 (risk-adapted biopsy decisions)
results.text: PSA density thresholds around 0.15-0.20 ng/mL/cc are associated with a higher probability of clinically significant cancer; low PSA density with negative or equivocal MRI identifies men at low risk who may safely avoid immediate biopsy.

results.source: Principles for AI-based clinical decision support
results.text: AI outputs should be presented with calibrated uncertainty, the evidence used, and known limitations; the treating clinician remains responsible for the decision, and uncertain cases should be escalated to multidisciplinary review.
